claims.text: Controlled pre-oxidation of an FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating induces a uniform nanoscale oxide layer.
The pre-oxidation-induced oxide forms along coating grain boundaries.
The pre-oxidation-induced oxide forms at the coating–substrate interface.
The nanoscale oxide layer acts as a protective barrier at high temperatures.
The oxide barrier reduces direct metal–metal contact during wear.
Reduced direct metal–metal contact lowers friction.
The oxide barrier mitigates abrasive interactions and thereby reduces wear.
An oxide layer that is too thick or discontinuous may crack or spall.
Oxide cracking or spallation increases wear.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have lower wear rates than as-deposited coatings at 300–600 °C when a critical, uniform oxide thickness is achieved.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have lower friction coefficients than as-deposited coatings at 300–600 °C when a critical, uniform oxide thickness is achieved.
The presence of a continuous nanoscale oxide film will correlate with improved wear resistance.
The proposed mechanism applies to sliding or abrasive wear at 300–600 °C.
Wear behavior may differ outside the specified temperature or loading range.
The oxide layer's stability may vary over extended wear cycles and near 600 °C.

contradictions.description: The predicted benefit is conditional on achieving a critical, uniform oxide layer, but absence of such a layer is itself designated as falsification. Failure to generate the stated prerequisite could instead reflect inadequate or unspecified pre-oxidation parameters, so it does not cleanly falsify the conditional wear mechanism.
